plan.why: Dept 3 accounts for most of the flagged gap and is well below forecast across most stores that week, so I'm checking for category-level or company-level stationery and back-to-school explanations, along with apparel and Texas-specific conditions for the next two largest gaps (Depts 23 and 49).

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

passages.section: Walmart U.S. Neighborhood Markets and Other Small Formats
passages.text: Fiscal Years Ended January 31, STRATEGIC MERCHANDISE UNITS 2013 2012 2011 Grocery 55% 55% 53% Entertainment 11% 12% 12% Health and wellness 11% 11% 11% Hardlines 9% 9% 9% Apparel 7% 7% 8% Home 7% 6% 7% Total 100% 100% 100% Periodically, we make revisions to the categorization of the components comprising our strategic merchandise units. When revisions are made, we also adjust the previous period's presentation to maintain comparability.

Retail Sales Retail sales growth softened over the reporting period, and sales are up slightly year-over-year. Sales in the Eleventh District continue to outperform the nation, according to two national retailers. Contacts noted that holiday hiring has begun or will begin soon, and hours worked are up from the previous report. Commodity input costs are easing, but the drought has caused prices for grains and feedstock to rise. The outlook for the rest of the retail quarter, which ends in October, is mixed but contacts are cautiously optimistic for the fourth quarter.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: We had positive comps across all geographies and store formats. During the quarter, we focused on being the destination for back-to-school and Halloween shopping. Our merchants and operators developed a strong cross-functional plan, and I'm pleased with our execution and the sales growth achieved this year. As a reminder, a slightly larger portion of Halloween sales versus last year will fall into the fourth quarter comp period, given how the 4-5-4 calendar falls this year.

The retail method requires management to make certain judgments and estimates that may significantly impact the ending inventory valuation at cost, as well as the amount of gross profit recognized. Judgments made include recording markdowns used to sell inventory and shrinkage. When management determines the salability of inventory has diminished, markdowns for clearance activity and the related cost impact are recorded. Factors considered in the determination of markdowns include current and anticipated demand, customer preferences and age of merchandise, as well as seasonal and fashion trends. Changes in weather patterns and customer preferences related to fashion trends could cause material changes in the amount and timing of markdowns from year to year.

• Health and wellness includes pharmacy, optical services and over-the-counter drugs. report.summary: Store 39's flagged departments were also well below the ML forecast at many other Texas stores and at most stores nationally in the week ending Sep 7, 2012. That pattern points to a shared cause, such as category demand or the calendar, rather than something only at this store. No report or outside factor names these departments for that week, so no specific cause is confirmed.

findings.title: Apparel and stationery drops shared across Texas
findings.text: All 13 other Texas stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 3 Stationery, and 13 of 13 in Dept 31 Accessories, so the drops are not unique to this store. Most Texas stores were also below the ML forecast in several apparel departments. This suggests a wider cause, though the cause is not verified.

findings.title: Stationery drop seen at most stores
findings.text: 36 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 3 Stationery that week, with a median of -44.1%. This store's -63.5% is large but sits within the range seen elsewhere. The ML team's notes describe a recent decline and a forecast that may be too high.

findings.title: Stamps drop is not typical nationally
findings.text: Only 22 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 60 Stamps / Service Plans, with a median of +0.1%. Store 39's -42.7% is therefore less common than the other departments, and it is one of the more local signals to check.

findings.title: Walmart overall near forecast that week
findings.text: All 45 stores together were $48,296,614 vs $48,462,259 forecast (-0.3%), which is close to the forecast. Store 39's overall total was $1,609,812 vs $1,722,405 forecast (-6.5%). Walmart's FY2013 Q3 comparable sales were +1.5%, which is a company-wide figure, not a figure for this store.

findings.title: Report context on Dallas sales and markdowns
findings.text: The Aug 29, 2012 Beige Book said that "Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up \"slightly.\"" Walmart's annual report says that "Changes in weather patterns and customer preferences related to fashion trends could cause material changes in the amount and timing of markdowns from year to year." These are general statements about the district and Walmart, not about this store or these departments.

report.not_found: No report, outside factor or store-only event was found that names these departments or this store for the week ending Sep 7, 2012.
next_steps: Check stationery and apparel stock on hand and recent deliveries for the week ending Sep 7, 2012, against what was received and sold.
Review whether apparel and stationery displays, end-cap placement or shelf prices changed in the weeks before Sep 7, 2012.
Check for local competitor promotions or events near the store around the Labor Day weekend.
Confirm staffing levels in the apparel and stationery areas for the week of Sep 7, 2012 compared with prior weeks.
Check how the Stamps / Service Plans sales were recorded that week, in case of a data entry or till issue.
Review the timing and department-level records of any markdowns, noting that the recorded markdowns of $35,329 are store-level only.
data_needed: Department-level inventory and delivery records for the flagged departments for the weeks before and after Sep 7, 2012.
Department-level sales for the same departments over the prior 8 to 12 weeks at this store.
Department-level markdown records, showing which departments the markdowns applied to and when.
Information on local competitor pricing or promotions near the store in late August and early September 2012.
Staffing and schedule records for the flagged departments for the same weeks.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: In the second quarter, we continued to see varying inflationary trends across the box. Within entertainment, deflation continues to impact sales growth in electronics. Total grocery inflation moderated slightly from what we reported in the first quarter. In categories with higher inflation, customers continued to trade down. We are also monitoring key commodities and the severe drought across parts of the country to gauge potential impact on food prices throughout the remainder of the year. Walmart is well positioned to serve our customers in this challenging market environment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

We compete with a number of companies for prime retail site locations, as well as in attracting and retaining quality employees (whom we call "associates"). We, along with other retail companies, are influenced by a number of factors including, but not limited to: general economic conditions, cost of goods, consumer disposable income, consumer debt levels and buying patterns, consumer credit availability, interest rates, tax rates, customer preferences, unemployment, labor costs, inflation, deflation, currency exchange rate fluctuations, fuel and energy prices, weather patterns, climate change, catastrophic events, competitive pressures and insurance costs. Further information on certain risks to our Company can be located in "Item 1A.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Grocery, which includes food and consumables, delivered a low single-digit positive comp for the quarter. Our focus on winning key seasonal events paid off as we saw very strong food sales around the Fourth of July holiday. Another big success this quarter has been our USDA Choice steak program. The program has helped drive sales to the entire meat department, which outperformed the overall food business by approximately 300 basis points in the second quarter. The unmatched combination of quality and value has resonated with a large number of our customers, including many who had not previously shopped our meat department.

Wages and Prices Price inflation was limited for most final goods and services during the reporting period. Prices increased for some energy items, mainly crude oil, retail gasoline, and electricity, but natural gas prices remained near historic lows. Contacts also noted price increases for assorted food commodities, particularly grains, although meat prices reportedly have leveled off for the time being. For most products and services, vigorous competition among firms and cost-conscious purchasing behavior by consumers kept price inflation in check.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. Retail Trade and Services Retail sales rose further overall. Contacts reported sales were a bit stronger relative to the prior reporting period. Discount chains and online retailers continued to outperform traditional department stores. At grocery stores, consumer spending was soft as shoppers continued to shift their purchasing decisions in favor of cheaper products. Contacts reported a strong pace for auto sales, significantly above the pace from the same period last year. Demand for used vehicles also remained robust.

Net sales for the Walmart U.S. segment increased 3.6% and 4.4% for the three and nine months ended October 31, 2012, respectively, when compared to the same periods in the previous year. The increases in net sales were due to increases in comparable store sales of 1.5% and 2.5% as a result of improved ticket and traffic for the three and nine months ended October 31, 2012, respectively, combined with year-over-year growth in retail square feet of 2.1%. Walmart U.S.'s focus on expanded merchandise assortment and price leadership were key factors contributing to the sales performance. Gross profit rate declined 30 and 25 basis points for the three and nine months ended October 31, 2012, respectively, compared to the same periods in the previous year.

passages.source: Walmart news release, 2012-07-18: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.section: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.text: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms BENTONVILLE, Ark., July 18, 2012 /PRNewswire/ -- Walmart today announced the results of the "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey," which revealed that 76 percent of moms with children in kindergarten to 12th grade consider back-to-school a time for a fresh start over Jan. 1[1] – in fact, nine out of ten moms make back-to-school "resolutions" in preparation for the year ahead[2]. With 78 percent of moms planning to get organized[3] this new school year, Walmart today launched Classrooms by Walmart, an online compilation of thousands of classroom supply lists representing schools in all 50 states plus Washington, D.C., making it easier for moms to get their back-to-school supplies online and in Walmart stores.

Forward-looking statements This release contains statements as to Walmart management's forecasts of the company's earnings per share for the fiscal quarter and fiscal year to end Jan. 31, 2013 (and certain assumptions underlying such forecasts), and management's expectations regarding the comparable store sales of the Walmart U.S. segment and comparable club sales, excluding fuel, of the Sam's Club segment of the company for the 13-week period from Oct. 27, 2012 through Jan. 25, 2013, and management's expectations that the Walmart U.S. operating segment will have strong performance through Thanksgiving weekend, that the company believes are "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended.

plan.why: The three largest dollar gaps (Sporting Goods $16,471, Stationery $10,601, Lawn & Garden $7,198) make up about $34k of the $60.9k flagged, and the cross-store comparison shows these drops were widespread across the chain that week (chain-wide -5.3%), so the queries check for category, Walmart-level, and regional explanations.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Comp sales in hardlines increased by low-single digits. We continue to see steady good performance in stationery, crafts, and sporting goods. Sporting goods had strong performance due to expanded hunting assortment, including guns and ammunition. The addition of key hardlines categories to layaway was attractive to customers, who also purchased items not on the layaway list.

Agriculture Drought conditions improved slightly due to scattered rainfall in July. Crops remained mostly in fair to good shape, with the exception of dryland cotton crop in the Texas High Plains region which suffered due to lack of moisture. Overall, crop conditions were much better than a year ago. Drought in the Midwest has caused grain prices to climb sharply, squeezing margins for ranchers by driving up feed costs for livestock.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.
Both Walmart U.S. and Sam's Club will report comp sales for the 13-week period on Feb. 21, 2013, when the company reports fourth quarter results.

Agriculture The District remained largely in drought, although scattered rainfall improved soil moisture conditions in several areas. Crops were mostly in fair to good shape. Production is expected to be better than last year--when the drought was much more severe in the Eleventh District--but below average because of ongoing dry conditions. Grain prices remained high due to the Midwest drought, adversely affecting Texas' large livestock sector as feed costs reached record highs.

The Atlanta and San Francisco reports noted that discount retailers performed better than traditional department stores, while the Chicago report attributed the pace of growth in consumer spending to heavy discounting by retailers clearing space for back-to-school items. Boston and Chicago reported continuing weakness in furniture sales; Boston also reported weak sales of electronics, but Chicago noted some improvement in this category. Adult clothing sold well in Boston, Chicago, and Dallas. The Atlanta District said that luxury goods merchants, while still largely positive, provided more mixed reports compared with earlier this year; Kansas City cited weaker sales for high-end jewelry.

report.summary: Store 6 was below the ML forecast in 17 flagged departments, and the same departments were also below forecast at many other stores and across Texas that week. Walmart overall and the Dallas Fed reports give only general context, and no passage names these departments for this week. The main possible reasons are shared, store-wide, or local, and none is verified.

findings.title: Chain-wide shortfall that week
findings.text: All 45 stores together were $44,169,616 against a $46,628,419 ML forecast (-5.3%), with 36 of 45 stores below forecast. Store 6 was -10.7% overall, a larger gap than the chain as a whole.

findings.title: Same departments short at many stores
findings.text: Dept 3 Stationery was below the ML forecast at 43 of 44 other stores, and Dept 9 Sporting Goods at 38 of 44. Texas showed the same pattern, with 13 of 13 other stores below for Dept 3 and 11 of 13 for Dept 9.

findings.title: Store-wide pattern across many departments
findings.text: Store 6 had 60 of its 70 departments below the ML forecast that week, so the gaps are not limited to the 17 flagged departments. This suggests a pattern across the store, though the cause is not identified.

findings.title: Reports point at general, not department-level, causes
findings.text: The Walmart earnings call said "Sporting goods had strong performance due to expanded hunting assortment" and described stationery as "steady good performance". The Oct 10, 2012 Beige Book noted that "rising gasoline prices" were among factors affecting sales, but it is a Texas-wide and national view and not specific to this store.

findings.title: Outside conditions only partly changed
findings.text: No holiday fell in this week. Local fuel was $3.72/gal against $3.63 in the prior four-week median, and temperature was 76°F against 85°F. Unemployment was 5.7%, the same as before.

departments.what_supports_it: Store 6 was $52,088 against a $68,558 ML forecast (-24.0%), the largest dollar gap in the flagged list. Texas showed the same pattern, with 11 of 13 other stores below forecast and 4 flagged. The ML notes say it was -26.3% against the median of the last 4 weeks, but the ML team's notes also say the model was too high at 86.4% of other stores.

Store 6 was $12,904 against a $23,505 ML forecast (-45.1%), one of the largest percentage gaps in the flagged list. Texas had 13 of 13 other stores below forecast, and 43 of 44 stores across the chain were below. The earnings call describes stationery as "steady good performance", which does not fit a drop this large.

Store 6 was $15,511 against a $22,709 ML forecast (-31.7%). Texas had 13 of 13 other stores below forecast, and 42 of 44 stores across the chain were below. The ML notes mention a seasonal decline of -21.0% against earlier years, which is the ML team's view, not a reported fact.

Store 6 was $1,255 against a $4,372 ML forecast (-71.3%), the largest percentage gap in the flagged list. Across the chain the median other store was -16.3%, so this store's gap is far larger, and in Texas 2 of 5 other stores were below forecast. No report or local data points at this department.

report.not_found: No report, holiday, or outside factor was found that names these departments or this store's local conditions for the week ending Sep 14, 2012.
next_steps: Check on-hand stock and recent deliveries for Dept 9, Dept 3, and Dept 16 against the sales drop.
Check whether Dept 9 has the expanded hunting and firearms assortment described in the earnings call, and whether it is on the shelf.
Check staffing and whether sporting goods, stationery, and lawn and garden were fully staffed that week.
Check pricing, price tags, and displays for the flagged departments in the week ending Sep 14, 2012.
Check for local events or nearby competitors' promotions that week, especially for Dept 58 Wireless Services.
Check data entry for Dept 58 Wireless Services and Dept 99 Store Supplies, which recorded $0 sales.
data_needed: Weekly department sales for Store 6 for the 8 weeks before Sep 14, 2012, to test whether the drop is new.
Stock on hand and delivery records by department for the week ending Sep 14, 2012.
Staffing schedules for the week ending Sep 14, 2012.
Local competitor pricing and promotion records for Sep 2012.
Department-level markdown records (only store-level markdowns of $24,970 across 5 fields are available, which cannot be tied to a department).

plan.why: Dept 3 has the largest dollar gap, and Depts 31 and 33 follow, so searches should test whether back-to-school timing, a cooler weather shift, and fuel-price pressure in the Gulf Coast explain the apparel and stationery drops.

passages.text: Natural Resources and Agriculture Contacts reported a renewed increase in production at Gulf Coast refineries because of recent closures along the East Coast. An increase in demand for crude oil and oil products, along with the Gulf Coast seeing particularly high demand for diesel fuels and other distillates, has helped to support refined product prices. Recent rains improved conditions in many parts of the District. Compared with the same time last year, prices paid to farmers for soybeans, corn, oranges, beef, hogs, and broilers were up while cotton was down. Although beef prices have increased over the last year, contacts reported that both the drought and high feed prices have resulted in lower prices paid to farmers on a month-over-month basis.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: We had positive comps across all geographies and store formats. During the quarter, we focused on being the destination for back-to-school and Halloween shopping. Our merchants and operators developed a strong cross-functional plan, and I'm pleased with our execution and the sales growth achieved this year. As a reminder, a slightly larger portion of Halloween sales versus last year will fall into the fourth quarter comp period, given how the 4-5-4 calendar falls this year.

report.summary: Several flagged departments also fell below the ML forecast at many other stores, especially Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear, Dept 6 Cameras and Dept 60 Stamps / Service Plans, which points to a wider pattern. Dept 3 Stationery and Dept 48 Firearms were lower at this store than at most other stores, so local causes are possible there. The ML team's notes and the outside factors are possible reasons only, and none of them has been verified.

findings.title: Outerwear and swimwear low at many stores
findings.text: 31 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear that week, and this store was at -39.1%. Cooler weather that week (76°F vs 82°F) is a possible reason for this category, but it has not been verified.

findings.title: Cameras, services and stamps also broadly low
findings.text: 27 of 38 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 6 Cameras, 33 of 44 in Dept 60 Stamps / Service Plans, and 15 of 22 in Dept 58 Wireless Services. The ML team's notes list recent and seasonal declines for these departments.

findings.title: Stationery and firearms lower than most stores
findings.text: Dept 3 Stationery was at -23.7% here, while only 9 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast there, so this drop is more local. Dept 48 Firearms was at -62.7% here, while 4 of 8 other stores were below its forecast, so the same check applies.

findings.title: Store overall below forecast, Walmart overall above
findings.text: 45 of 69 of this store's departments were below the ML forecast, and the store as a whole was $2,124,176 against a $2,186,742 forecast (-2.9%). Across all 45 stores that week, sales were $47,427,672 against a $47,131,573 forecast (+0.6%).

findings.title: Dallas Fed report points the other way
findings.text: The Dallas Fed Beige Book (Aug 29, 2012) says "Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel." This describes the district as a whole, not this store, and it does not explain the flagged drops in those same categories here.

departments.what_supports_it: This store was at -23.7%, while only 9 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast. That points to a possible local cause such as stock or deliveries, but none was found in the data.
31 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast that week, and this store was at -39.1%. The drop is shared across stores, and the cooler temperature is a possible reason.
This store was at -58.9%, and Store 34 in the same region was flagged at -57.5%. Only one other store in the region is in the data, so this is limited regional evidence.
27 of 38 other stores were below the ML forecast, so the drop is broad, though this store's -45.6% is still below the median of the other stores (-15.3%).
This store was at -62.7%, which is the third-lowest of 9 stores, while only 4 of 8 other stores were below the forecast. The ML team notes a recent decline and that the forecast may be too high.

report.not_found: I looked for a shared regional pattern, a holiday, and store-level notes on stock, staffing or events, and found none beyond the Gulf Coast comparison (only one other store) and the outside factors listed.
next_steps: Check stock on hand and recent deliveries for Dept 3 Stationery and Dept 48 Firearms.
Check stock levels and the weather-related sales plan for Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear.
Review staffing and sales floor coverage in the apparel departments for the week of Aug 24, 2012.
Check pricing, displays and markdown records for the store this week (markdowns are recorded for the whole store, so they cannot be tied to one department).
Look for local events or competitor activity that could affect Dept 6 Cameras and Dept 58 Wireless Services.
Confirm that this week's department sales were entered correctly at the store.

report.summary: Across all Walmart stores, sales that week were close to the ML forecast, but the flagged departments were below forecast at many stores, including every other Texas store in several of them. Dept 3 Stationery, Dept 24 Boyswear and Dept 31 Accessories show the largest gaps here. No single cause has been confirmed; the regional pattern, the Labor Day week and store-side stock or staffing are possible reasons to check.

passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Customers are responding favorably to the message, which is running in 25 metro markets. We're proud that we do so well competitively on the basket challenges. passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: So, let's get on to our results. Mike Duke will kick off the news for the third quarter. M
passages.text: Walmart U.S. posted a comp sales increase of 1.5 percent, and delivered approximately $2.3 billion in net sales growth. Back to school activities drove sales early in the quarter, and the mid-September launch of layaway was important in helping customers. Operating income outpaced net sales growth for the quarter and was a key driver of our overall company profit. Bill and his team are executing very innovative plans to drive traffic and to help America's families have a great holiday season. That's what our customers expect and we will deliver. We announced our extended Black Friday program, and customers are already working on their shopping lists.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

Retail Trade and Services Retail sales rose further overall. Contacts reported sales were a bit stronger relative to the prior reporting period. Discount chains and online retailers continued to outperform traditional department stores. At grocery stores, consumer spending was soft as shoppers continued to shift their purchasing decisions in favor of cheaper products. Contacts reported a strong pace for auto sales, significantly above the pace from the same period last year. Demand for used vehicles also remained robust.

passages.text: The Atlanta and San Francisco reports noted that discount retailers performed better than traditional department stores, while the Chicago report attributed the pace of growth in consumer spending to heavy discounting by retailers clearing space for back-to-school items. Boston and Chicago reported continuing weakness in furniture sales; Boston also reported weak sales of electronics, but Chicago noted some improvement in this category. Adult clothing sold well in Boston, Chicago, and Dallas. The Atlanta District said that luxury goods merchants, while still largely positive, provided more mixed reports compared with earlier this year; Kansas City cited weaker sales for high-end jewelry.

EX-99.1 d440140dex991.htm PRESS RELEASE Press Release Exhibit 99.1 For Immediate Release Media Relations Contact Randy Hargrove 800-331-0085 Investor Relations Contact Carol Schumacher 479-277-1498 Pre-recorded conference call 877-523-5612 (U.S. and Canada) 201-689-8483 (All other countries) Call passcode: 9256278 Walmart reports Q3 EPS of $1.08, reaffirms top end of full-year EPS guidance; Company is well positioned for Q4 holidays Q3 Highlights : Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. (Walmart) reported third quarter diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $1.08, within guidance of $1.04 to $1.09. This was an 11.3 percent increase from the $0.97 per share reported for the third quarter last year.

Forward-looking statements This release contains statements as to Walmart management's forecasts of the company's earnings per share for the fiscal quarter and fiscal year to end Jan. 31, 2013 (and certain assumptions underlying such forecasts), and management's expectations regarding the comparable store sales of the Walmart U.S. segment and comparable club sales, excluding fuel, of the Sam's Club segment of the company for the 13-week period from Oct. 27, 2012 through Jan. 25, 2013, and management's expectations that the Walmart U.S. operating segment will have strong performance through Thanksgiving weekend, that the company believes are "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended.

Comparable store and club sales in the U.S., including fuel, increased 2.4% and 1.6% in fiscal 2013 and 2012 , respectively, when compared to the previous fiscal year. U.S. comparable store and club sales increased during fiscal 2013 as a result of improved average ticket and an increase in customer traffic. U.S. comparable store sales increased during fiscal 2012 primarily due to an increase in average ticket, partially offset by a decline in traffic, while comparable club sales were higher due to a larger member base driving increased traffic, as well as a broader assortment of items. As we continue to add new stores and clubs in the U.S., we do so with an understanding that additional stores and clubs may take sales away from existing units. We estimate the negative impact on comparable store and club sales as a result of opening new stores and clubs was approximately 0.7% in fiscal 2013 and 0.8% in fiscal 2012 .

Retail Trade and Services Retail sales expanded a bit further overall. Respondents in general indicated that sales strengthened somewhat in July compared with softness in May and June. Performance was stronger for discount chains than traditional department stores, particularly for online sales. At grocery stores, extensive bargain hunting by shoppers caused sales revenues to weaken a bit. The pace of auto sales slowed somewhat compared with the prior reporting period, although it remained significantly above the pace from the same period last year. Used vehicles have been in short supply, raising their trade-in values and helping to spur sales of new vehicles.

report.summary: In the week ending Aug 10, 2012, Store 10 sold $1,880,411 against a $1,899,152 ML forecast (-1.0%). Several flagged drops are shared widely across stores, such as Outerwear & Swimwear and Media, while Boyswear and Girlswear fell much further here than at other stores. These are possible explanations only, not verified causes.

findings.title: Outerwear drop seen at most stores
findings.text: Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 34 of 36 other stores that week, with a median of -36.6%. The store's -34.0% is in line with that chain-wide pattern, and the temperature was 91°F against a 85°F median for the four prior weeks, which may be relevant.

findings.title: Media and Jewelry also fell at many stores
findings.text: Media (expanded) was below the ML forecast at 32 of 36 other stores, and Jewelry at 29 of 42. A Fed report noted weaker high-end jewelry sales in one district, though it did not cover this region.

findings.title: Boyswear and Girlswear fell far more here
findings.text: Boyswear was 41.2% below the ML forecast here, while 7 of 36 other stores were below in that department, with a median of +12.5%. Girlswear showed a similar gap at this store, and the ML team's notes list seasonal decline as a signal, which is the ML team's own view.

findings.title: Accessories drop mixed across the region
findings.text: In the West Coast region, 3 of 5 other stores were also flagged in Accessories, including Store 42 at -84.5%. The region shows a shared pattern here, but this store's -45.8% is not an outlier in the group.

findings.title: Chain and district sales context
findings.text: Walmart's overall sales for the week were $47,386,845 against a $47,102,033 forecast (+0.6%), and the Walmart U.S. comparable sales for FY2013 Q3 were +1.5%. A San Francisco Fed report said "Respondents in general indicated that sales strengthened somewhat in July compared with softness in May and June."

findings.title: Store-wide markdowns cannot be tied
findings.text: Store-wide markdowns of $35,706 were recorded this week. They apply to the whole store and cannot be linked to any single department, so they do not explain these department drops.

departments.what_supports_it: This store was 41.1% below the ML forecast, far more than the 7 of 36 other stores in this department that were below forecast. The ML team's notes show a -24.3% gap against the same season in earlier years.
This store was 34.6% below the ML forecast, while 7 of 36 other stores were below forecast with a median of +13.4%. The ML notes point to recent and seasonal decline.
3 of 5 West Coast stores were also flagged, so a regional pattern is possible. This store's -45.8% gap is the largest in the department's shown ranking.
34 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast, with a median of -36.6%. The temperature being higher than the prior weeks may be relevant.
32 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast, with a median of -7.8%. This suggests a broad drop rather than a local one.
29 of 42 other stores were below the ML forecast, though the median was only -5.4%. A Fed report noted weaker high-end jewelry sales in another district.

report.not_found: The data was searched for a holiday, a shared regional cause, and store-side records on stock, staffing, pricing or local events for Boyswear and Girlswear; none were found, and no store-side records are included.

passages.text: Natural Resources and Agriculture Contacts reported a renewed increase in production at Gulf Coast refineries because of recent closures along the East Coast. An increase in demand for crude oil and oil products, along with the Gulf Coast seeing particularly high demand for diesel fuels and other distillates, has helped to support refined product prices. Recent rains improved conditions in many parts of the District. Compared with the same time last year, prices paid to farmers for soybeans, corn, oranges, beef, hogs, and broilers were up while cotton was down. Although beef prices have increased over the last year, contacts reported that both the drought and high feed prices have resulted in lower prices paid to farmers on a month-over-month basis.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: We had positive comps across all geographies and store formats. During the quarter, we focused on being the destination for back-to-school and Halloween shopping. Our merchants and operators developed a strong cross-functional plan, and I'm pleased with our execution and the sales growth achieved this year. As a reminder, a slightly larger portion of Halloween sales versus last year will fall into the fourth quarter comp period, given how the 4-5-4 calendar falls this year.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Customers are responding favorably to the message, which is running in 25 metro markets. We're proud that we do so well competitively on the basket challenges. Keep in mind these are actual baskets the customer has purchased, not just a key item comparison. We're also pleased with the sales and traffic results versus control markets. Our customers appreciate value, especially in uncertain economic times. We'll continue to lead on price through the back-to-school season and into the second half of the year. Now, I'd like to discuss the details of our second quarter performance.

findings.title: Home storage drop seen at most stores

findings.title: Store Supplies down at every other store

findings.title: Walmart-wide week was below forecast
findings.text: Across all 45 stores, sales were $47,131,887 against a $48,409,634 forecast (-2.6%), and 35 of 45 stores were below the forecast. Walmart's quarter reported U.S. comparable sales of +1.5%.

findings.title: Auto Services drop is local to this store

findings.title: Weather and fuel changed that week

findings.title: Atlanta District report notes slower sales
findings.text: The Federal Reserve Beige Book of Aug 29, 2012 says "In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales". This describes the district as a whole, not this store, and it does not name these departments.

passages.text: Price pressures were said to be contained as most Districts reported that both finished goods and input prices were little changed since the last report. Higher prices were cited by some Districts for agricultural commodities and petroleum-based products, although low or declining natural gas prices were reported in the Atlanta, Kansas City, Dallas, and San Francisco Districts. Contacts in the Atlanta, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts noted that drought conditions continued to result in higher feed prices. There were scattered reports of higher crop prices starting to show through to food prices at the consumer level. Atlanta reported an increase in corn and soybean prices, while Chicago and Kansas City reported that these prices declined somewhat. Slightly lower prices for some technology-related products were reported in the San Francisco District.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: We had positive comps across all geographies and store formats. During the quarter, we focused on being the destination for back-to-school and Halloween shopping. Our merchants and operators developed a strong cross-functional plan, and I'm pleased with our execution and the sales growth achieved this year. As a reminder, a slightly larger portion of Halloween sales versus last year will fall into the fourth quarter comp period, given how the 4-5-4 calendar falls this year.

Natural Resources and Agriculture Contacts reported a renewed increase in production at Gulf Coast refineries because of recent closures along the East Coast. An increase in demand for crude oil and oil products, along with the Gulf Coast seeing particularly high demand for diesel fuels and other distillates, has helped to support refined product prices. Recent rains improved conditions in many parts of the District. Compared with the same time last year, prices paid to farmers for soybeans, corn, oranges, beef, hogs, and broilers were up while cotton was down. Although beef prices have increased over the last year, contacts reported that both the drought and high feed prices have resulted in lower prices paid to farmers on a month-over-month basis.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: So, let's get on to our results. Mike Duke will kick off the news for the third quarter. M
passages.text: Walmart U.S. posted a comp sales increase of 1.5 percent, and delivered approximately $2.3 billion in net sales growth. Back to school activities drove sales early in the quarter, and the mid-September launch of layaway was important in helping customers. Operating income outpaced net sales growth for the quarter and was a key driver of our overall company profit. Bill and his team are executing very innovative plans to drive traffic and to help America's families have a great holiday season. That's what our customers expect and we will deliver. We announced our extended Black Friday program, and customers are already working on their shopping lists.

passages.text: EX-99.1 d440140dex991.htm PRESS RELEASE Press Release Exhibit 99.1 For Immediate Release Media Relations Contact Randy Hargrove 800-331-0085 Investor Relations Contact Carol Schumacher 479-277-1498 Pre-recorded conference call 877-523-5612 (U.S. and Canada) 201-689-8483 (All other countries) Call passcode: 9256278 Walmart reports Q3 EPS of $1.08, reaffirms top end of full-year EPS guidance; Company is well positioned for Q4 holidays Q3 Highlights : Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. (Walmart) reported third quarter diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $1.08, within guidance of $1.04 to $1.09. This was an 11.3 percent increase from the $0.97 per share reported for the third quarter last year.

passages.section: Walmart U.S. Neighborhood Markets and Other Small Formats
passages.text: Fiscal Years Ended January 31, STRATEGIC MERCHANDISE UNITS 2013 2012 2011 Grocery 55% 55% 53% Entertainment 11% 12% 12% Health and wellness 11% 11% 11% Hardlines 9% 9% 9% Apparel 7% 7% 8% Home 7% 6% 7% Total 100% 100% 100% Periodically, we make revisions to the categorization of the components comprising our strategic merchandise units. When revisions are made, we also adjust the previous period's presentation to maintain comparability.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Hello, this is Carol Schumacher, vice president of investor relations for Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. Thanks for joining us today for our earnings call to review the third quarter of fiscal 2013. All information for this quarter, including our unit counts, square footage, and financial metrics, is available on our website. New address: stock.walmart.com. Please note that while we update unit counts on a monthly basis on our website, in the earnings discussion today, units and square footage are referred to as of the quarter end. Our press release is available on the website, and a full transcript of this call has already been posted there. Here's the agenda for today's call.
Both Walmart U.S. and Sam's Club will report comp sales for the 13-week period on Feb. 21, 2013, when the company reports fourth quarter results.

report.summary: Several apparel and other departments sold below the ML forecast at many Texas stores and across the chain that week, so the drops look shared rather than local to Store 2. The week was also below forecast for Walmart overall, and no holiday or report names these departments as falling. These are the ML team's estimates, not verified losses, and no specific cause has been confirmed.

findings.title: Apparel drops seen across Texas stores
findings.text: At Texas stores, Girlswear was below the ML forecast at 10 of 10 other stores, and Outerwear & Swimwear at 10 of 10, with 7 and 9 of those flagged. Plus & Maternity was below at 8 of 10 other Texas stores.

findings.title: Several departments below forecast chain-wide
findings.text: Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 31 of 36 other stores that week, with a median of -36.1%. Store Supplies was below at all 14 other stores, and Optical at 25 of 31.

findings.title: Walmart overall was below forecast that week
findings.text: All 45 stores together sold $47,131,887 against a $48,409,634 forecast (-2.6%), with 35 of 45 stores below. For the full quarter, Walmart U.S. comparable sales were +1.5%.

findings.title: Regional report points to apparel strength
findings.text: The Dallas Fed Beige Book of Aug 29, 2012 said "Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel." This describes the district in general and does not explain the drops at this store, and it also says "Inventories were lighter than desired."

findings.title: Store overall near forecast; no holiday
findings.text: Store 2 as a whole was $1,946,501 against $1,950,556 forecast (-0.2%), with 41 of 70 departments below. Store-wide markdowns of $35,230 are recorded for the whole store and cannot be tied to any one department. No holiday fell that week, and the local fuel price was $3.64/gal against $3.53 and the temperature was 83°F against 87°F.

departments.what_supports_it: 37 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast that week, and 10 of 13 Texas stores were too, though none of those were flagged. Store 2 was at -21.6%, the ML team's note says the model was too high at 84.1% of other stores.
25 of 31 other stores were below the ML forecast, and 4 of 10 Texas stores were flagged. The ML team notes a recent decline of -29.0% against the last 4 weeks' median.

19 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast, with 7 flagged, and 7 of 10 Texas stores were below. The ML team's notes show it was up against the last 4 weeks (+10.1%) and against the same season in earlier years (+17.4%).

Texas was the strongest pattern here: all 10 other Texas stores were below the ML forecast, with 7 flagged, and 23 of 36 stores overall were below. The ML team's notes show it was above the same season in earlier years (+14.5%).

31 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast, with a median of -36.1%, and all 10 Texas stores were below, 9 of them flagged. The ML team notes a recent decline of -27.9% against the last 4 weeks' median.
26 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast, and 5 of 10 Texas stores were flagged. The ML team notes a seasonal decline against the same season in earlier years of -31.9%.

report.not_found: I looked for a holiday, a local event, or a Walmart or Dallas Fed report that names these departments as falling, and found none; the Dallas Fed report points the other way for apparel.

Check whether any apparel or optical deliveries were late or short that week.
Review apparel and optical staffing and any open positions that week.
Check the pricing, signage, and displays for these departments, and whether any were moved or removed.
Ask the store team whether a nearby competitor ran apparel or optical promotions that week.
Confirm the department sales figures entered for the week ending Aug 31, 2012 match the register totals.

Staffing schedules for the apparel and optical departments
Local competitor pricing and promotion records for Texas apparel and optical

passages.text: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms BENTONVILLE, Ark., July 18, 2012 /PRNewswire/ -- Walmart today announced the results of the "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey," which revealed that 76 percent of moms with children in kindergarten to 12th grade consider back-to-school a time for a fresh start over Jan. 1[1] – in fact, nine out of ten moms make back-to-school "resolutions" in preparation for the year ahead[2]. With 78 percent of moms planning to get organized[3] this new school year, Walmart today launched Classrooms by Walmart, an online compilation of thousands of classroom supply lists representing schools in all 50 states plus Washington, D.C., making it easier for moms to get their back-to-school supplies online and in Walmart stores.

Builders noted strong traffic and reported rising backlogs, while realtors said shrinking inventories had led to price gains. Apartment demand remained strong, and contacts noted rising construction activity as investors continue to be attracted to the market. Housing outlooks remain positive.

report.summary: Store 11's 14 flagged departments were below the ML forecast for the week ending Aug 31, 2012, with $23,366 below forecast (an ML estimate, not a verified loss). The same departments were also below forecast at many other stores, including all or most Texas stores, and Walmart overall was below forecast that week. No cause specific to this store was found, and the shared pattern is a possible reason, not a confirmed one.

findings.title: Walmart overall was below forecast
findings.text: Across all 45 stores that week, sales were $47,131,887 against a forecast of $48,409,634 (-2.6%), and 35 of 45 stores were below forecast. Walmart's comparable sales for FY2013 Q3 were +1.5%.

findings.title: Apparel and home departments down at many stores
findings.text: Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 31 of 36 other stores, and at all 10 Texas stores. Dept 33 Girlswear, Dept 31 Accessories, and Dept 20 Domestics / Bath were also below forecast at most other stores, so this store's drops are part of a wider pattern.

findings.title: ML notes cite recent and seasonal declines

findings.title: Regional hardware demand held steady
findings.text: The Dallas Fed Beige Book for Aug 29, 2012 says: "Overall demand for construction-related products held steady or edged up since the last report." This describes the whole district, not this store, and it does not explain a drop, but it is the only regional report that touches the hardware departments. Dept 11 Hardware was below forecast at 32 of 44 other stores.

findings.title: Outside factors changed little
findings.text: There was no holiday that week. Local fuel prices were $3.64/gal against $3.53 in the prior four weeks, temperature was 86°F against 87°F, and unemployment was 6.3% in both periods. None of these is a clear reason for the drops.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most District merchants reported that sales growth remained slow in September. Discount retail operations outperformed traditional department stores. Most retailers projected continued soft growth in sales through the end of 2012. Contacts in the auto industry reported that strong sales levels were maintained in September.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.
Both Walmart U.S. and Sam's Club will report comp sales for the 13-week period on Feb. 21, 2013, when the company reports fourth quarter results.

findings.title: Furniture and Lawn & Garden drops seen elsewhere
findings.text: Furniture was below the ML forecast at 29 of 36 other stores that week (median -13.9%), and Lawn & Garden at 38 of 44 (median -12.6%). Store 4's drops in these departments were larger, at -37.5% and -26.4%.

findings.title: Store-wide and Walmart-wide below forecast
findings.text: All 45 stores sold $43,589,549 against a $44,444,458 forecast (-1.9%), and 33 of 45 stores were below forecast. At Store 4, 54 of 71 departments were below forecast, and the store total was $2,027,620 vs $2,096,925 forecast (-3.3%).

findings.title: Regional report notes slow sales growth
findings.text: The Oct 10, 2012 Beige Book for the Atlanta Fed District reported that "Most District merchants reported that sales growth remained slow in September." The national section notes "rising gasoline prices" and weather among factors affecting sales, which may be a general context for softer sales, though this is not confirmed for Store 4.

findings.title: Cameras drop not shared by other stores
findings.text: Cameras at other stores were mostly above forecast (median +11.1%), so Store 4's -33.2% is not explained by a broad trend. The only other store in the region with this department was Store 34 at -46.7%, which is based on one store.

findings.title: ML notes show recent and seasonal declines
findings.text: The ML team's notes list a recent decline and a seasonal decline for Furniture. Its notes also say the forecast was higher than actual sales at 80.6% of other stores. Store-level markdowns of $17,027 were recorded for the whole store and cannot be tied to any department.

departments.what_supports_it: 29 of 36 other stores were below forecast in this department that week, with a median of -13.9%. Store 4 was -37.5%, the largest drop in its flagged departments, and the ML notes show recent and seasonal declines.
38 of 44 other stores were below forecast (median -12.6%), so the category was weak broadly. Store 4 was -26.4%, and the ML notes show recent and seasonal declines.

27 of 37 other stores were below forecast (median -5.4%), a moderate broad softness. Store 4 was -21.7%, the largest drop in its Home department group after Furniture and Lawn & Garden, and its ML notes show a recent decline.
Other stores were mostly above forecast (median +11.1%), so the drop looks more local to Store 4 at -33.2%. This is the department to check first on the store side.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Most of our merchandising areas again delivered solid performance, though industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category. We're seeing market share growth across grocery and health & wellness. You can expect to hear more about market share and how we're using Nielsen data during our annual analyst meeting in October.

Prices Most reporting firms said prices were steady. Several contacts in the transportation services industry noted higher diesel prices led to higher costs. Shipping firms expect higher ground and air prices as a result. Airline industry contacts noted that business travelers were very price sensitive and soft demand was keeping a lid on fares. Food and cattle producers noted price increases due to continued commodity price pressures.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

(Walmart) reported third quarter diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $1.08, within guidance of $1.04 to $1.09. This was an 11.3 percent increase from the $0.97 per share reported for the third quarter last year.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Home, including seasonal categories, had a low single-digit positive comp. Our continued focus on basics, supported by strong item merchandising and a refined assortment, drove strong performance in the quarter. Indoor living, led by cooking and dining, again performed well, as most departments posted an increased comp versus the first quarter. Back-to-school and back-to-college shopping is well under way. Our stores were ready to serve shoppers early in the season, and we're pleased with the results. Season to date, key back-to-school apparel categories are up 7.0 percent. Within home, we're seeing strong performance in college essentials like bedding and bath.

Price pressures were said to be contained as most Districts reported that both finished goods and input prices were little changed since the last report. Higher prices were cited by some Districts for agricultural commodities and petroleum-based products, although low or declining natural gas prices were reported in the Atlanta, Kansas City, Dallas, and San Francisco Districts. Contacts in the Atlanta, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts noted that drought conditions continued to result in higher feed prices. There were scattered reports of higher crop prices starting to show through to food prices at the consumer level. Atlanta reported an increase in corn and soybean prices, while Chicago and Kansas City reported that these prices declined somewhat. Slightly lower prices for some technology-related products were reported in the San Francisco District.

report.summary: Most of the flagged departments were also below the ML forecast at many other Texas and other stores that week, so the pattern is shared rather than limited to this store. Walmart overall was also below its forecast that week, which may point to a wider category or calendar cause. The ML team's estimate of $22,961 below forecast is not a verified loss, and no store-side cause has been confirmed.

findings.title: Entertainment drops shared across many stores
findings.text: Media & Gaming was below the ML forecast at 41 of 44 other stores that week, and Texas stores in Cameras and Photo Lab also fell below their forecasts. This suggests a shared category pattern, not a problem only at this store.

findings.title: Outerwear and Swimwear fell chain-wide
findings.text: 31 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast in Outerwear & Swimwear, with a median of -32.9%, and all 10 other Texas stores were below too. The ML team's notes say this department had a recent decline and a seasonal decline.

findings.title: Girlswear shared, Boyswear more local
findings.text: 23 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast in Girlswear, and Boyswear was below at only 19 of 36 stores, with a median of -1.2%. This makes Boyswear's drop at this store (-25.3%) look more specific to this store, although the data does not show why.

findings.title: Walmart overall below forecast that week
findings.text: All 45 stores together sold $47,131,887 against a $48,409,634 forecast (-2.6%), with 35 of 45 stores below. Walmart's U.S. comparable sales for FY2013 Q3 were +1.5%, and no holiday fell in this week.

findings.title: Store-wide gap and unlinked markdowns
findings.text: This store was $1,577,148 against a $1,598,715 forecast (-1.3%), with 52 of 69 departments below forecast. Markdowns of $41,608 were recorded for the whole store, but they cannot be tied to any one department.

findings.title: Walmart cites entertainment category pressure
findings.text: In the Aug 16, 2012 earnings call, Walmart said "industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category." This is company-wide context and does not name this store or these exact departments.

passages.text: Similarly, weekly attendance and revenues at Broadway theaters were running ahead of comparable 2011 levels in August and early September but slipped well below year-earlier levels for the third week of the month. Finally, consumer confidence fell in August and was little changed at a low level in September, according to the Conference Board's monthly survey of residents of the Middle Atlantic states (NY, NJ, Pa).

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has remained flat in recent weeks. A major retail chain reports that sales in the region were sluggish in August and especially in September, running well below comparable 2011 levels. Some of the weakness is attributed to unseasonably mild weather, which dampened sales of seasonal merchandise. A major mall in upstate New York describes sales activity as "stagnant", with sales flat to down slightly from a year ago in August and September. The pricing environment is described as quite promotional, and acquisition costs of goods are characterized as mostly stable to declining modestly. Auto dealers in upstate New York report steady sales activity. New vehicle sales were up 6-9 percent from a year earlier in August but are projected to be flat to up slightly in September. Sales of used cars have been mixed since the last report, while dealers' service departments note some slowing in business. Wholesale and retail credit conditions remain favorable.

passages.text: Retail Sales Retail sales growth softened over the reporting period, and sales are up slightly year-over-year. Sales in the Eleventh District continue to outperform the nation, according to two national retailers. Contacts noted that holiday hiring has begun or will begin soon, and hours worked are up from the previous report. Commodity input costs are easing, but the drought has caused prices for grains and feedstock to rise. The outlook for the rest of the retail quarter, which ends in October, is mixed but contacts are cautiously optimistic for the fourth quarter.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Comp sales in hardlines increased by low-single digits. We continue to see steady good performance in stationery, crafts, and sporting goods. Sporting goods had strong performance due to expanded hunting assortment, including guns and ammunition. The addition of key hardlines categories to layaway was attractive to customers, who also purchased items not on the layaway list.

Petrochemicals producers noted Gulf Coast chemical production was up slightly, but uncertainty cautioned firms' outlooks. Gulf Coast refiners said they were operating at rates above 90 percent, and strong export demand was keeping inventories from building. Retail Sales Retailers said demand was mixed over the past six weeks. Sales in the Eleventh District continued to outperform the nation, according to two national retailers. Contacts said the loss in sales resulting from Hurricane Sandy was temporary and would not impact holiday spending. Outlooks through year-end were mixed.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

plan.why: The three largest dollar gaps (media $3,996, girlswear $2,867, hardware $2,696) are the departments most likely to reflect a category-wide or regional demand shift, which Walmart's quarterly results and the Dallas Fed reports could confirm or rule out.

passages.text: The Atlanta and San Francisco reports noted that discount retailers performed better than traditional department stores, while the Chicago report attributed the pace of growth in consumer spending to heavy discounting by retailers clearing space for back-to-school items. Boston and Chicago reported continuing weakness in furniture sales; Boston also reported weak sales of electronics, but Chicago noted some improvement in this category. Adult clothing sold well in Boston, Chicago, and Dallas. The Atlanta District said that luxury goods merchants, while still largely positive, provided more mixed reports compared with earlier this year; Kansas City cited weaker sales for high-end jewelry.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Comp sales in technology and entertainment, which continued to experience deflation, were slightly positive this quarter. Wireless, up double-digit comps, performed well and benefitted from both the Samsung Galaxy III and the Apple iPhone 5. Televisions and home theater comps are up low single-digit, driven by unit movement and improved availability in large screen televisions. Average selling prices continue to decrease for TVs, and our inventory position for the holidays is very good. Video games, music and movies continue to experience pressure in the current environment.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. Sales growth in the Eleventh District remained stronger than the nation, on average, according to two large retailers. Retailers expect a seasonal pickup in demand in the fourth quarter, although sales will likely be down from last year. Automobile sales were mostly flat since the last report, but were up from year ago levels. Inventories were lighter than desired. Contacts said political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious.

report.summary: Most of the flagged departments were also below the ML forecast at many other stores that week, so the drops look wider than this store alone. The store's total was $1,373,641 against a $1,438,399 forecast (-4.5%), and no holiday fell that week. No store-specific cause was found in the data provided, so the possible reasons below are not verified.

findings.title: Media & Gaming fell at most stores
findings.text: Dept 5 Media & Gaming sold $12,112 against a $16,108 ML forecast (-24.8%), and 41 of 44 other stores were also below forecast in this department that week. findings.title: Store-wide and national totals were also lower

report.summary: Store 6 was below the ML forecast in most of its departments for the week ending Jul 27, 2012, and the drop was also seen across Walmart's 45 stores and in Texas. The largest gaps are in Dept 5 Media & Gaming and Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear, where many other stores were also below forecast. These are possible shared reasons, not verified causes, and no store-only explanation was found in the data provided.

findings.title: Entertainment category pressure noted by Walmart
findings.text: The Aug 16, 2012 earnings call said "industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category." This may relate to the Dept 5 Media & Gaming and Dept 55 Media (expanded) gaps, but the report does not mention these departments or this store.

findings.title: Walmart-wide shortfall in the same week
findings.text: Across all 45 stores that week, sales were $44,084,063 against a $46,419,912 forecast (-5.0%), and 43 of 45 stores were below the forecast. This suggests a wider pattern, not only a problem at Store 6.

findings.title: Outerwear dropped at most stores and in Texas
findings.text: In Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear, 35 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast, with a median of -36.9%. Store 6 was -40.5%, and 9 of 10 Texas peers were also below forecast. Warmer weather that week (86°F vs 82°F) may be a possible factor, though the data does not link the two directly.

findings.title: Texas stores also below forecast in several departments
findings.text: In Texas, 10 of 13 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 5 Media & Gaming, and 9 of 10 were below in Dept 55 Media (expanded). Store 6 is in the same region, so a shared regional factor is possible, but the data does not name one.

findings.title: Store-wide drop across most departments
findings.text: Store 6 sold $1,513,228 against a $1,623,605 forecast (-6.8%), and 55 of its 70 departments were below the ML forecast. The six flagged departments make up only part of this wider pattern.

findings.title: Dallas Fed notes sales strength and cautious outlook
findings.text: The Aug 29, 2012 Beige Book said "Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago" and that "political uncertainty was hampering consumer confidence, and outlooks were cautious." It also noted "Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel," which does not clearly match the Outerwear drop.

departments.what_supports_it: Actual sales were $22,391 against a $29,732 ML forecast (-24.7%). 37 of 44 other stores were below forecast that week, and the entertainment category is mentioned in the Walmart earnings call.
Actual sales were $4,089 against a $6,873 ML forecast (-40.5%). 35 of 36 other stores were also below forecast, and the warmer week may be a possible factor.
Actual sales were $9,311 against an $11,851 ML forecast (-21.4%). 30 of 36 other stores were below forecast, and it is in the same entertainment unit as Dept 5.
Actual sales were $2,025 against a $3,706 ML forecast (-45.4%). 13 of 22 other stores were below forecast, but the median drop elsewhere was -13.5%, so the gap is larger than most stores.
Actual sales were $1,609 against a $2,144 ML forecast (-24.9%). Most other stores were not below forecast (median -0.8%), so this gap is more specific to Store 6 and the Texas stores that were down.
Actual sales were $6 against a $72 ML forecast (-91.7%). The amounts are very small, and the department name and unit are unresolved, so this may be a data issue rather than a sales pattern.

report.not_found: No report, outside factor, or store-level record was found that explains a department drop at Store 6, and markdowns were recorded only for the whole store ($27,721), so they cannot be linked to any department.
