passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

Agriculture Drought conditions improved slightly due to scattered rainfall in July. Crops remained mostly in fair to good shape, with the exception of dryland cotton crop in the Texas High Plains region which suffered due to lack of moisture. Overall, crop conditions were much better than a year ago. Drought in the Midwest has caused grain prices to climb sharply, squeezing margins for ranchers by driving up feed costs for livestock.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Demand for paper products held steady, and contacts said they expect modest sales growth for the year. Food producers said sales activity increased over the past six weeks and orders were up significantly from year-ago levels. One food manufacturer reported adding several new workers in part due to strong demand. Automobile and aviation equipment manufacturers said demand held steady since the last report. Expectations are for seasonal pickup in automobile sales over the summer, but aviation manufacturers expect sales to remain flat.

report.summary: In the week ending Aug 3, 2012, several of Store 6's flagged departments fell below the ML forecast in the same departments at many other stores, especially in Texas for Outerwear & Swimwear and Horticulture. Walmart overall was close to its forecast that week (-0.4%), and there was no holiday. No report names these departments, so the reasons below are possible explanations, not confirmed causes.

findings.title: Lawn & Garden fell below forecast chain-wide
findings.text: 38 of 44 other stores were also below the ML forecast in Lawn & Garden that week, with a median of -12.9%. Store 6's gap was the largest of its flagged departments, at -19.9%.

findings.title: Outerwear drop widespread across Texas
findings.text: 35 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast in Outerwear & Swimwear, and 7 Texas stores were flagged in this department too. Store 6 was at -35.9%, against a store threshold of -19.0%.

findings.title: Horticulture down at nearly every Texas store
findings.text: All 11 other Texas stores were below the ML forecast in Horticulture, and 10 of them were flagged. Store 6 was at -29.7%. The ML team's notes say the model was too high at 89.5% of other stores.

findings.title: Store-wide shortfall across many departments
findings.text: 50 of Store 6's 69 departments were below the ML forecast that week. The store as a whole was $1,627,252 against $1,676,050, or -2.9%, compared with -0.4% for all 45 stores together.

findings.title: Weather and fuel changed; no holiday
findings.text: The temperature was 88°F against a 4-week median of 82°F, and fuel was $3.42/gal against $3.28. Unemployment was unchanged at 5.7%. These are possible background factors for seasonal departments, not confirmed causes.

findings.title: Dallas retail spending reported slightly up
findings.text: The Aug 29, 2012 Beige Book said that Dallas retail sales were up "slightly" in July and early August. This is general regional context and does not mention these departments or this store.

departments.what_supports_it: Store 6 recorded $28,912 against an ML forecast of $36,074, a $7,162 gap (-19.9%). 38 of 44 other stores were also below forecast in this department, but no Texas store was flagged. The ML team's notes list a -14.3% change against the median of the last 4 weeks.
Store 6 was at -35.9%, and the median for other stores was -45.8%. 32 other stores were flagged, including 7 in Texas. The ML team's notes list a -53.3% change against the median of the last 4 weeks.
Store 6 was at -27.3%, and 28 of 39 other stores were below forecast with a median of -16.9%. 6 Texas stores were flagged in this department.
Store 6 was at -35.4%, and 28 of 36 other stores were below forecast with a median of -15.3%. 2 Texas stores were flagged in this department.
Store 6 was at -44.4%, and 5 of 6 other stores were below forecast with a median of -42.4%. Only one other Texas store was in the comparison, and it was above forecast (+26.9%).
Store 6 was at -29.7%. 34 of 38 other stores were below forecast, and all 11 Texas stores were below, with 10 flagged.

report.not_found: I looked for a holiday, a Walmart or Fed report naming these departments, Texas, or Store 6, and a local event, and found none for this week.
next_steps: Check stock levels and deliveries for Lawn & Garden, Outerwear & Swimwear and Horticulture for the week ending Aug 3, 2012.
Check staffing schedules for the same week, especially in the apparel and seasonal areas.
Check whether Lawn & Garden, Outerwear, Horticulture and Firearms had displays, price changes or stockouts that week.
Check for local competitor promotions or local events in the week before and during Aug 3, 2012.
Review the $53,920 of store-wide markdowns recorded that week and when they started; they are not tied to any department in the data.
Confirm that the department sales figures entered for Store 6 that week match the register records.

Staffing and hours by department for the same weeks.
Department-level price and display change logs for the same weeks.
Local competitor promotion records for the Store 6 trade area.

passages.text: EX-99.1 d440140dex991.htm PRESS RELEASE Press Release Exhibit 99.1 For Immediate Release Media Relations Contact Randy Hargrove 800-331-0085 Investor Relations Contact Carol Schumacher 479-277-1498 Pre-recorded conference call 877-523-5612 (U.S. and Canada) 201-689-8483 (All other countries) Call passcode: 9256278 Walmart reports Q3 EPS of $1.08, reaffirms top end of full-year EPS guidance; Company is well positioned for Q4 holidays Q3 Highlights : Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. (Walmart) reported third quarter diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $1.08, within guidance of $1.04 to $1.09. This was an 11.3 percent increase from the $0.97 per share reported for the third quarter last year.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. report.summary: Outerwear & Swimwear and Plus & Maternity were below the ML forecast at most stores that week, which points to a category-wide pattern. Ladieswear and Sleepwear were below forecast at this store more than at most others, and the store as a whole was 4.8% below forecast, so local causes are also possible. No single cause is confirmed.

findings.title: Outerwear and swimwear down at most stores
findings.text: Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 35 of 36 other stores that week, with a median of -44.9%. The weather was cooler than the week before (75°F vs 79°F), which may be one possible reason.

findings.title: Plus & Maternity also down at most stores
findings.text: Plus & Maternity was below the ML forecast at 28 of 36 other stores, with a median of -15.3%. This store's -40.5% is larger than that median, but the drop is not unique to this store.

findings.title: Store-wide softness across many departments
findings.text: This store had 47 of 68 departments below the ML forecast, and the store as a whole was $1,704,696 against $1,789,823 (-4.8%). Markdowns recorded for the whole store that week were $68,200, but they cannot be linked to any one department.

findings.title: Ladieswear and Sleepwear mostly local
findings.text: Ladieswear was -24.0% at this store, but the median at other stores was only -1.4%. Sleepwear / Underwear was -20.6%, while the median at other stores was +1.3%, so this store is lower than most. The ML team's notes describe a recent decline for both.

findings.title: Walmart overall close to forecast
findings.text: Across all 45 stores that week, sales were $47,466,798 against a $47,656,239 forecast (-0.4%). Walmart reported U.S. comparable sales of +1.5% for the quarter, and its earnings call said apparel had posted a low single-digit comp increase, so the drop does not look like a company-wide shortfall.

findings.title: New York sales firmed, apparel prices steady
findings.text: A Fed report from Aug 29, 2012 said "Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August." It also said "Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices". This points away from a broad regional apparel slump.

departments.what_supports_it: This is the largest dollar gap ($4,626, -24.0%). 21 of 36 other stores were also below the ML forecast, but the median was only -1.4%, so this store is lower than most. The ML team's notes describe a recent decline and a seasonal decline.

This is the largest percentage gap (-75.5%). 35 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast, with a median of -44.9%, which points to a category-wide drop. The cooler week (75°F vs 79°F) may be one possible reason.
This is -40.5%, with 28 of 36 other stores also below the ML forecast (median -15.3%). The ML team's notes say the model was too high at most other stores.

This is -26.6% ($2,963). In the same region, 2 of 3 other stores were flagged, but across all stores the median was +4.7%, so the pattern is mixed. The ML team's notes describe a recent decline and a seasonal decline.
This is -20.6% ($2,086). 17 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast, but the median was +1.3%, so this store is an outlier. The ML team's notes describe a recent decline.

report.not_found: No report, outside factor or other store data was found that explains why this store's departments fell below the ML forecast, beyond the weather and category patterns above; no local stock, staffing, or competitor records were provided.
next_steps: Check stock levels and recent deliveries for Outerwear & Swimwear and Plus & Maternity against what was on the floor that week.
Review apparel displays, pricing and any markdown activity that week in those departments, recognizing the store-wide markdown total cannot be assigned to one department.
Check whether staffing or hours in the apparel areas changed in late July or early August.
Check for local events, new nearby competitors, or promotions that week.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Health and wellness continues to be a key traffic driver as well and overall delivered a mid single-digit comp increase. Hearing aid centers achieved double-digit comps for the quarter. We had mid single-digit comps in OTC and low single-digit comps in prescriptions. Like Walmart U.S., the recent availability of popular prescriptions that have moved from branded to generic status negatively impacted overall sales, but drove profitability and unit volume. Rx script count was up mid single-digits, and we expect this trend to continue.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported modest increases in retail spending on a year-over-year basis, but many reported slower growth in recent months compared with earlier in the year; however, Boston and Cleveland reported sales as flat, and New York cited softer sales. There were a few reports that high summer temperatures negatively affected sales. Sales of big-ticket household goods were strong in the Richmond, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts, while sales were reportedly flat for home furnishings and major appliances in the San Francisco District. Boston reported that sales for furniture and electronics had slowed, and retailers in the New York District reported that home goods sales were weak. Reports from luxury-goods retailers were mixed.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Retail Sales Retail sales increased but the pace of growth decelerated slightly compared to earlier in the year. Sales of apparel, bedding, household items, and small furniture fared well. Discount retailers said sales of food and sundries continued to perform the strongest. Overall sales growth in the Eleventh District continued to outpace the nation, on average, according to three large retailers. Outlooks are cautiously optimistic and contacts say it appears as if the environment has improved slightly for the consumer. Automobile sales continued to grow at a steady pace. Inventories were at desired levels and prices remained stable. Auto dealers expect sales growth to continue at the same pace through year end.

report.summary: Store 21 sold $692,959 against a $723,002 forecast for the week ending Aug 3, 2012, with 12 departments flagged. Several flagged departments also fell below forecast at many other stores, which points to wider causes, while Bakery and Service Deli fell much further here than elsewhere. These are possible reasons only, and no cause is verified.

findings.title: Pharmacy fell much further here
findings.text: Pharmacy was 26.2% below forecast here, while the median of other stores was +2.0%. A Walmart report dated Aug 16, 2012 (after this week) says "the recent availability of popular prescriptions that have moved from branded to generic status negatively impacted overall sales," which is a possible wider reason but is Walmart-wide and not specific to this store.

findings.title: Horticulture and outerwear dropped widely
findings.text: Horticulture was below forecast at 34 of 38 other stores, and Outerwear & Swimwear was below at 35 of 36, so these drops are shared across stores rather than local. Temperatures were 92°F vs 85°F the prior 4-week median, and a Fed report says "There were a few reports that high summer temperatures negatively affected sales."

findings.title: Bedding fell here but not elsewhere
findings.text: Bedding was 25.9% below forecast here, but only 8 of 37 other stores were below forecast (median +9.6%). A Dallas Fed report from Jul 18, 2012 says "Sales of apparel, bedding, household items, and small furniture fared well," which does not point to a wider bedding decline.

findings.title: Bakery and Service Deli low here
findings.text: Store 21 as a whole was 4.2% below forecast, with 51 of 65 departments below. Bakery was 85.5% below forecast and Service Deli 62.0% below, far beyond the other stores' medians of -8.6% and -5.3%.

findings.title: Chain-wide week was close to forecast
findings.text: Across all 45 stores, sales were 0.4% below forecast that week, and Walmart reported +1.5% U.S. comparable sales for FY2013 Q3. The large drops are therefore mostly department-specific rather than a store-wide or chain-wide shortfall.

departments.what_supports_it: The Walmart report mentions prescription sales being hurt by the move of popular drugs from branded to generic status, which may partly explain softness, though it is not specific to this store. The ML team's notes list a seasonal decline.
Only 2 of 10 Texas stores were below forecast in this department, and a July Dallas Fed report said bedding sales fared well. The ML team's notes list recent and seasonal declines.
35 of 36 other stores were also below forecast, and the ML team's notes list recent and seasonal declines. Warm weather that week (92°F vs 85°F) may be a possible factor.
34 of 38 other stores were below forecast, with all 11 Texas peers below. Warm weather (92°F vs 85°F) and the ML team's notes on seasonal decline are possible reasons.

The drop here (-85.5%) is far larger than the store-level median of -8.6%, and Texas stores were also below forecast, though by much smaller amounts. Store-side causes such as deliveries or staffing are not shown in the data.

passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Sales growth in the quarter was well balanced, with positive comps across all 3 geographic business units and in all of our store formats. Our 1.4 million associates did an outstanding job serving our customers, and I'm particularly pleased with the results we achieved during the key holiday events of Mother's Day, Father's Day and the Fourth of July. Despite a midweek holiday, July 4th sales, especially in key categories like food, significantly exceeded our expectations.

Petrochemicals producers reported steady demand. Demand for PVC, tied to residential construction, improved domestically, and exports continued to be a major source of sales. Exports of caustic soda remained strong as U.S. prices are very competitive due to lower electricity costs. Chlorine demand edged up, while demand for propylene weakened. Gulf Coast refiners said operating rates remained high at 90 percent. Robust export demand for gasoline and distillates kept inventories low, and refiners' margins remained healthy.

passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Speaking of apparel, our momentum continued in the second quarter. I'm proud of the work that the team has done, and I'm very happy to say that our focus on basics is working. For the quarter, we delivered a low single-digit positive comp, our second consecutive quarter of positive comps. Our customers continue to turn to Walmart for their basics, a key element of our apparel strategy that is built around jeans, underwear, socks and tees. You see this executed in every store. In the second quarter, we had solid results in ladies' and men's departments, as well as positive comps in shoes, which benefitted from the addition of new brands.

Natural Resources and Agriculture Contacts reported a renewed increase in production at Gulf Coast refineries because of recent closures along the East Coast. An increase in demand for crude oil and oil products, along with the Gulf Coast seeing particularly high demand for diesel fuels and other distillates, has helped to support refined product prices. Recent rains improved conditions in many parts of the District. Compared with the same time last year, prices paid to farmers for soybeans, corn, oranges, beef, hogs, and broilers were up while cotton was down. Although beef prices have increased over the last year, contacts reported that both the drought and high feed prices have resulted in lower prices paid to farmers on a month-over-month basis.

passages.section: Now, I'll turn the program over to Charles for our wrap-up and guidance. Charles …
passages.text: The first goal: Walmart U.S. must continue its momentum. Walmart U.S. is delivering a broad assortment at the lowest price, and you heard today that customers continue to respond well. With the right mix of local relevance in every store, the breadth of assortment allows us to take better care of our customers. We have now delivered positive comp sales for four consecutive quarters. Our marketing is reinforcing our strong price positioning and we believe this places us in a great position for the third and fourth quarters.

Retail Trade and Services Retail sales expanded a bit further overall. Respondents in general indicated that sales strengthened somewhat in July compared with softness in May and June. Performance was stronger for discount chains than traditional department stores, particularly for online sales. At grocery stores, extensive bargain hunting by shoppers caused sales revenues to weaken a bit. The pace of auto sales slowed somewhat compared with the prior reporting period, although it remained significantly above the pace from the same period last year. Used vehicles have been in short supply, raising their trade-in values and helping to spur sales of new vehicles.

report.summary: Toys, Media & Gaming, and Outerwear & Swimwear were below the ML forecast at most other stores in the week ending Jul 27, 2012, so part of the pattern looks wider than this store. Produce and Optical were mostly below the ML forecast only at this store. No Walmart or Fed report found names these departments, so any cause below is a possibility, not a confirmed one.

findings.title: Toys and media fell at most stores
findings.text: Toys was below the ML forecast at 40 of 44 other stores that week, with a median of -11.7%. Media & Gaming was below at 37 of 44 other stores, with a median of -13.6%. This points to a drop shared across many stores, not only this one.

findings.title: Outerwear and swimwear fell almost everywhere
findings.text: Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 35 of 36 other stores, with a median of -40.4%. The week was hotter than usual at 93°F vs 90°F, which could be one possible link, but no report was found that ties this to the department.

findings.title: Produce and Optical dropped mainly here
findings.text: Produce was at $2 against a $118 ML forecast here, while other stores had a median of -5.1%. Optical was -49.3% here, while other stores had a median of -0.5%. Most of this store's gap in these two departments appears local to this store, and the ML team's notes on Optical say the forecast may be too high.

findings.title: Walmart and district trends were mixed
findings.text: The Beige Book reported that "At grocery stores, extensive bargain hunting by shoppers caused sales revenues to weaken a bit" in the San Francisco Fed District. That describes district grocery stores in general, not this store, and it is only a possible background for the Produce gap.

findings.title: Store-wide gap spread across departments
findings.text: Store 12 had 51 of 66 departments below the ML forecast that week, and the store as a whole was $916,966 vs $970,795 forecast. Store-level markdowns of $22,980 were recorded, but they cannot be tied to any single department.

departments.what_supports_it: Toys was below the ML forecast at 40 of 44 other stores that week, and the ML team's note says the drop was -4.2% against the same season in earlier years. The region also shows drops at Store 33 and Store 42.
Media & Gaming was below the ML forecast at 37 of 44 other stores, and all 5 other West Coast stores were below. The ML team's note says the drop was -30.2% against the same season in earlier years.
Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 35 of 36 other stores, with a median of -40.4%. The week's temperature of 93°F vs 90°F is a possible but unverified link.
Produce was far below at this store but close to the forecast at most other stores, with a median of -5.1%. The Beige Book's grocery comment is only general background and not a confirmed cause.
Optical was -49.3% here, while the other stores had a median of -0.5%. The ML team's notes say the forecast may be too high, and no report was found that explains this store's drop.

report.not_found: No report, passage, or outside factor was found that specifically explains the drops in these five departments at this store in the week ending Jul 27, 2012.
next_steps: Check Produce stock on hand and deliveries for the week ending Jul 27, 2012, and whether any Produce orders were missed.
Check Optical staffing and whether the department was open, stocked, and displayed as usual that week.
Check Toys and Media & Gaming shelf and display changes, and any local competitor promotions in the week.
Check Outerwear & Swimwear floor space and stock against the hot weather that week.
Check the store's sales register and department coding for the flagged departments in case of data entry errors.

Delivery and order records for Produce and Optical for the same week.
Staffing schedules for Optical and the department floor for the week.
Records of local competitor promotions or events near the store that week.
Department-level markdown records, if they exist, to check whether the store-level markdown total can be tied to any department.

passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Most of our merchandising areas again delivered solid performance, though industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category. We're seeing market share growth across grocery and health & wellness. You can expect to hear more about market share and how we're using Nielsen data during our annual analyst meeting in October.

Retail Sales Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period and were up from a year ago. Particular strength was seen in sales of accessories, cosmetics and women's and children's apparel. report.summary: Store 11's flagged drops were mostly in apparel and home departments, and many other stores, including several in Texas, show the same kind of drop in those departments that week. The store as a whole was close to its ML forecast, and the Dallas Fed report points to slight retail sales growth, so the pattern looks department-specific rather than store-wide. The $10,821 total is an ML estimate of sales below the ML forecast, not a verified loss.

findings.title: Outerwear and horticulture fell at most stores
findings.text: Outerwear & Swimwear was below the ML forecast at 35 of 36 other stores that week, with a median of -45.8%. Horticulture was below the ML forecast at 34 of 38 other stores, with a median of -30.4%. Store 11's drops in both departments were smaller than the typical drop elsewhere.

findings.title: Texas stores show similar cameras and horticulture drops
findings.text: In Texas, 8 of 11 other stores were below the ML forecast for Cameras, and 6 of those were flagged. In Horticulture, all 11 other Texas stores were below the ML forecast, and 10 were flagged. These are the ML team's flags, not verified causes.

findings.title: Store total close to forecast; drop is by department
findings.text: Store 11 as a whole was $1,399,144 against a forecast of $1,399,827, and 40 of its 68 departments were below the ML forecast. Across all 45 stores, the total was $47,466,798 against a forecast of $47,656,239.

findings.title: Hot week and Dallas retail context
findings.text: Temperature was 87°F that week against 83°F in the four weeks before, and there was no holiday. Walmart's Q3 comparable sales growth was +1.5%. A hotter week could affect outerwear sales, but no report confirms this.

findings.title: Dallas Fed notes lighter inventories
findings.text: The Dallas Fed Beige Book of Aug 29, 2012 said "Retail sales grew slightly over the reporting period" and "Inventories were lighter than desired." This describes the Dallas district as a whole, not Store 11, so it cannot show what happened in this store's departments.

findings.title: ML notes describe recent and seasonal declines
findings.text: The ML team's notes list a recent decline for Cameras and Horticulture and a seasonal decline for Jewelry. The notes also say the model ran above actual sales at most other stores in several departments. These are the ML team's notes only and are not verified.

departments.what_supports_it: This is the largest dollar gap at $3,007 (-21.6%), but the median store was only -3.6% below forecast, so the drop looks more local. In Texas, 3 flagged stores (Store 30 -47.2%, Store 37 -44.0%, Store 43 -25.0%) were the largest drops.
Store 11 was $2,218 (-23.4%) below forecast, and 30 of 42 other stores were also below forecast, with a median of -10.1%. The ML notes mention a seasonal decline, but no report confirms this.
Store 11 was -49.8% below forecast, and 6 of 8 Texas stores below forecast were flagged. The ML notes mention a recent decline and a seasonal decline, which fit the wider pattern.
Store 11 was -30.4% below forecast, which is milder than the -45.8% median across other stores. The hotter week may be relevant, but no report confirms it.
Store 11 was -24.8% below forecast, and 27 of 38 other stores were also flagged. This is a widespread drop, so it may point to a wider cause rather than a problem at this store alone.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has been somewhat softer since the last report. One major retail chain indicates that sales were down noticeably from a year earlier, with home goods sales especially weak. Another major chain reports that sales slowed in June and were running somewhat below plan but still up marginally from a year earlier; however, some improvement was noted during the first few days of July. Retail contacts in upstate New York report that sales were mixed in May but picked up in June, again buoyed by Canadian shoppers. Retail prices continue to be described as steady. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most District merchants reported that sales growth remained slow in September. Discount retail operations outperformed traditional department stores. Most retailers projected continued soft growth in sales through the end of 2012. Contacts in the auto industry reported that strong sales levels were maintained in September.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Comp sales in technology and entertainment, which continued to experience deflation, were slightly positive this quarter. Wireless, up double-digit comps, performed well and benefitted from both the Samsung Galaxy III and the Apple iPhone 5. Televisions and home theater comps are up low single-digit, driven by unit movement and improved availability in large screen televisions. Average selling prices continue to decrease for TVs, and our inventory position for the holidays is very good. Video games, music and movies continue to experience pressure in the current environment.

In media and gaming, we're well positioned for a very strong release schedule throughout the fourth quarter. report.summary: Outerwear & Swimwear and Lawn & Garden also fell below the ML forecast at most other Walmart stores that week, so a wider cause is possible for those two. Wireless Services and Stamps / Service Plans fell further at this store than at most others, so a local cause is possible for those two. Nothing in the outside factors or the reports clearly explains the store's shortfall.

findings.title: Outerwear drop seen at most stores
findings.text: 34 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast in Outerwear & Swimwear that week, with a median of -36.6%. This store's -30.8% is in line with that wider pattern, so a shared category or seasonal cause is possible.

findings.title: Lawn & Garden drop mostly at other stores
findings.text: 31 of 44 other stores were below the ML forecast in Lawn & Garden, with a median of -8.7%. In New England, 2 of the 5 other stores were above the ML forecast, so the drop is not uniform across the region.

findings.title: Wireless and Stamps drops look more local
findings.text: Wireless Services fell -42.6% here against a median of -14.4% at other stores, and Stamps / Service Plans fell -55.8% against a median of -6.1%. Most of the drop in these two departments is larger than at other stores, so a local cause is possible.

findings.title: Store-wide spread of shortfalls
findings.text: 40 of this store's 67 departments were below the ML forecast that week, but the store as a whole was only -1.0% below its forecast. Walmart overall was +0.6% that week.

findings.title: Outside factors show little change
findings.text: There was no holiday that week, and unemployment was steady at 4.2%. Fuel rose to $3.77/gal from $3.65 and temperature was 71°F against 70°F, which are small changes.

findings.title: Regional report on adult clothing demand
findings.text: The Boston Fed report says "Demand remains strong for adult clothing" in the district as a whole. This does not explain the Outerwear drop, and it describes the district, not this store.

report.summary: Store 12 had 11 departments below the ML forecast in the week ending Aug 3, 2012, with $7,401 below forecast (an ML estimate, not a verified figure). Two of the flagged departments, Outerwear & Swimwear and Horticulture, were also below forecast at most other stores that week, which points to a wider category pattern. Several other flags, such as Wireless Services and the small grocery departments, look more specific to this store.

findings.title: Outerwear & Swimwear down widely
findings.text: 35 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast in this department that week, with a median of -44.9%. This store was -46.4%, so the drop looks broadly shared rather than local. The ML team's notes mention a recent decline and a seasonal decline.

findings.title: Horticulture down at most stores
findings.text: 34 of 38 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 56 Horticulture that week, with a median of -30.4%. This store was -21.6%, which fits a shared pattern across stores.

findings.title: Jewelry drop also seen in the region
findings.text: In the West Coast (PADD 5) region, 4 of 5 other stores were below the ML forecast in Dept 32 Jewelry, and 3 of them were flagged. Across all stores, 30 of 42 were below, though the median was -10.1%, so this store's -22.4% is larger than most.

findings.title: Grocery drops look specific to this store
findings.text: Other stores were mostly near forecast in Dept 49 Optical (median +4.7%) and Dept 94 Produce (median -6.1%), while this store was far below in both. Possible local reasons include stock, displays, or how the small sales figures were entered, and the actual sales in these departments are very small.

findings.title: Overall retail spending reported up
findings.text: The Federal Reserve Beige Book of Aug 29, 2012 said "Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book." Walmart's store total that week was -0.4% against the ML forecast, with 20 of 45 stores below, so the wider backdrop does not explain Store 12's larger drops.

Video games, music and movies continue to experience pressure in the current environment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported modest increases in retail spending on a year-over-year basis, but many reported slower growth in recent months compared with earlier in the year; however, Boston and Cleveland reported sales as flat, and New York cited softer sales. Food producers said sales activity increased over the past six weeks and orders were up significantly from year-ago levels. One food manufacturer reported adding several new workers in part due to strong demand. Automobile and aviation equipment manufacturers said demand held steady since the last report. Expectations are for seasonal pickup in automobile sales over the summer, but aviation manufacturers expect sales to remain flat.

passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Most of our merchandising areas again delivered solid performance, though industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category. passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Our entertainment business had a low single-digit negative comp. While industry dynamics continued to pressure media and gaming, demand for tablets and tablet accessories remains strong. Customers continue to seek out the exclusive Walmart Straight Talk offering and our expanded assortment of smart phones. Straight Talk prepaid phones posted strong double-digit comp growth in the second quarter. We also introduced a solutions-focused merchandising approach that drove stronger printer and ink sales.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Health & wellness continued its trend, generating a low single-digit positive comp. Over the counter remained very strong as our broad assortment and continued focus on opening price point drove traffic gains and unit growth. Customers are finding value in our broader assortment of active nutrition products like whey protein and meal supplement bars. As expected, brand to generic conversions continued to pressure top-line sales, but conversions of Lipitor and other brands continue to improve pharmacy margins.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Comp sales in technology and entertainment, which continued to experience deflation, were slightly positive this quarter. Wireless, up double-digit comps, performed well and benefitted from both the Samsung Galaxy III and the Apple iPhone 5. Televisions and home theater comps are up low single-digit, driven by unit movement and improved availability in large screen televisions. Average selling prices continue to decrease for TVs, and our inventory position for the holidays is very good. Video games, music and movies continue to experience pressure in the current environment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

report.summary: The flagged departments are mostly ones that fell below the ML forecast at many other stores in the same week ending Aug 31, 2012. passages.source: Walmart news release, 2012-07-18: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.section: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.text: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms BENTONVILLE, Ark., July 18, 2012 /PRNewswire/ -- Walmart today announced the results of the "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey," which revealed that 76 percent of moms with children in kindergarten to 12th grade consider back-to-school a time for a fresh start over Jan. 1[1] – in fact, nine out of ten moms make back-to-school "resolutions" in preparation for the year ahead[2]. With 78 percent of moms planning to get organized[3] this new school year, Walmart today launched Classrooms by Walmart, an online compilation of thousands of classroom supply lists representing schools in all 50 states plus Washington, D.C., making it easier for moms to get their back-to-school supplies online and in Walmart stores.

Forward-looking statements This release contains statements as to Walmart management's forecasts of the company's earnings per share for the fiscal quarter and fiscal year to end Jan. 31, 2013 (and certain assumptions underlying such forecasts), and management's expectations regarding the comparable store sales of the Walmart U.S. segment and comparable club sales, excluding fuel, of the Sam's Club segment of the company for the 13-week period from Oct. 27, 2012 through Jan. 25, 2013, and management's expectations that the Walmart U.S. operating segment will have strong performance through Thanksgiving weekend, that the company believes are "forward-looking statements" within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

Retail and Tourism First District retail contacts offer a very mixed take on economic conditions in the region. Demand remains strong for adult clothing, but spending on durable items such as furniture and electronics continues to be lower than earlier in the year. Some companies cite disappointing sales during the last six weeks, while others report some upside surprises. Sales results range from low single-digit declines to high single-digit increases compared with a year earlier. Some contacts say that consumer sentiment has become more negative, while others observe that consumers are "coming back." Retailers note wholesale prices remain flat so they are holding selling prices steady. Respondents still express uncertainty about the direction of the U.S. economy and say they expect little improvement over the next six to eight months.

report.summary: Furniture is the flagged department with the clearest outside support: a Boston Fed report from Aug 29, 2012 describes weaker durable goods spending in the district. Store 22 was below the ML forecast in 51 of 65 departments, and the store-wide gap (-4.5%) was wider than Walmart's (-2.6%), so the flags look partly store-wide. Infant Apparel and Licensed Sports Apparel have no matching report, and the store-level markdown total cannot be tied to any department.

findings.title: Furniture matches a district report
findings.text: The Boston Fed Beige Book for Aug 29, 2012 says "spending on durable items such as furniture and electronics continues to be lower than earlier in the year." This fits the Furniture drop, though the report describes the district as a whole, not this store. The ML team's own notes also list a recent decline and a seasonal decline for this department.

findings.title: Sports apparel drop is regional and sharper here
findings.text: Four of the five other New England stores were also below the ML forecast in Licensed Sports Apparel, and two of them were flagged. Across all stores, however, the median was above the forecast (+13.8%), so the drop here looks more local than national.

findings.title: Infant Apparel drop is broad but deeper here
findings.text: Twenty-five of 39 other stores were below the ML forecast in Infant Apparel that week, with a median of -6.1%. Store 22 was at -23.9%, so the drop is wider than most stores, although the same department was soft across the chain. The Walmart Q3 earnings call described the apparel business as positive, which does not match the size of this store's gap.

findings.title: Store-wide shortfall beyond these four departments
findings.text: Store 22 was $1,021,776 against a $1,069,991 forecast (-4.5%), and 51 of 65 departments were below the ML forecast. Markdowns of $46,936 were recorded for the whole store that week, but they cannot be linked to any department, so they cannot explain these drops.

findings.title: Outside factors show only small changes
findings.text: No holiday fell in the week. Fuel was $3.88/gal against $3.81, temperature was 72°F against 74°F, and unemployment held at 7.8%. These are small changes and do not point clearly to any of the four departments.

departments.what_supports_it: This department had the largest dollar gap ($2,560), and 25 of 39 other stores were also below the ML forecast that week. The national apparel comment in the Walmart earnings call is general and does not name infant clothing.

Twenty-six of 42 other stores were below the ML forecast, and this store was at -24.9%, just past the -23.1% threshold. The ML notes show it was above its recent four-week median but below the same season in earlier years, and no report names accessories.
The Boston Fed report for Aug 29, 2012 describes weaker furniture spending in the district. The ML notes show a recent decline and a seasonal decline, and this store was at -26.1%.

This store was at -45.2%, the second-largest percentage gap, and four of five New England stores were also below the ML forecast. Across all stores the median was above forecast, and no report names this category.

passages.text: Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Most of our merchandising areas again delivered solid performance, though industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category. We're seeing market share growth across grocery and health & wellness. You can expect to hear more about market share and how we're using Nielsen data during our annual analyst meeting in October.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported modest increases in retail spending on a year-over-year basis, but many reported slower growth in recent months compared with earlier in the year; however, Boston and Cleveland reported sales as flat, and New York cited softer sales. There were a few reports that high summer temperatures negatively affected sales. Sales of big-ticket household goods were strong in the Richmond, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts, while sales were reportedly flat for home furnishings and major appliances in the San Francisco District. Boston reported that sales for furniture and electronics had slowed, and retailers in the New York District reported that home goods sales were weak. Reports from luxury-goods retailers were mixed.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Hello, this is Carol Schumacher, vice president of investor relations for Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. Thanks for joining us today for our earnings call to review the third quarter of fiscal 2013. All information for this quarter, including our unit counts, square footage, and financial metrics, is available on our website. New address: stock.walmart.com. Please note that while we update unit counts on a monthly basis on our website, in the earnings discussion today, units and square footage are referred to as of the quarter end. Our press release is available on the website, and a full transcript of this call has already been posted there. Here's the agenda for today's call.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

In the U.S., higher interest rates, higher fuel and other energy costs, weakness in the housing market, inflation, deflation, increased costs of essential services, such as medical care and utilities, higher levels of unemployment, decreases in consumer disposable income, unavailability of consumer credit, higher consumer debt levels, fluctuations in currency exchange rates, higher tax rates, imposition of new taxes and surcharges, other changes in tax laws, other regulatory changes, overall economic slowdown and other economic factors could adversely affect consumer demand for the products and services we sell through our Walmart U.S. segment and Sam's Club segment, change the mix of products we sell to one with a lower average gross margin, cause a slowdown in discretionary purchases of goods and result in slower inventory turnover and greater markdowns on inventory.

report.summary: Most of the flagged drops are shared by many other stores, especially Outerwear & Swimwear and Horticulture, which points to a wider category or seasonal cause. Wireless Services is the exception: other stores sold above the ML forecast that week, so its drop looks local to this store. Walmart's overall week was close to its forecast, and no cause has been verified.

findings.title: Outerwear drop shared by almost all stores
findings.text: 35 of 36 other stores were also below the ML forecast in Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear that week, with a median of -45.8%. This store's -33.6% is in the middle of that group, which suggests a category-wide pattern rather than a local problem.

findings.title: Cameras drop matches electronics slowdown reports
findings.text: Dept 6 Cameras was below the ML forecast at 28 of 39 other stores, and all 4 stores in the Central Atlantic region were below too. A Walmart report says "industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category" (Aug 16, 2012), and a Fed report from Jul 18, 2012 says Boston reported "sales for furniture and electronics had slowed." These are general reports and do not describe this store.

findings.title: Summer temperature may have affected sales
findings.text: A Fed report from Jul 18, 2012 says "high summer temperatures negatively affected sales," but it describes districts in general. The week of Aug 3, 2012 was 75°F against 77°F in the four prior weeks, a small difference. This may be relevant to Dept 56 Horticulture, where 34 of 38 other stores were also below the ML forecast.

findings.title: Wireless and Crafts look local to this store
findings.text: Other stores in Dept 58 Wireless Services were on average above the ML forecast (median +19.5%), so this store's -22.8% stands out. Dept 52 Crafts was also much weaker here (-27.3%) than at other stores (median -8.1%). The ML team's notes say the store-wide total was -1.0% and 39 of 70 departments were below forecast, so these two drops are not part of a store-wide decline.

findings.title: Walmart week near forecast; markdowns store-level only
findings.text: Across all 45 stores, sales were -0.4% against forecast, and 20 of 45 stores were below it, so the week was close to normal overall. The store recorded $60,519 in markdowns for the whole store, but these cannot be tied to any single department, so they cannot explain these drops.

departments.what_supports_it: This store was -31.3% below the ML forecast, the largest dollar gap ($2,426). Three of the four other Central Atlantic stores were also flagged, and the electronics slowdown mentioned in the Walmart and Fed reports fits the category.
The second-largest gap ($1,444) is unusual: other stores were a median +19.5% above forecast, so the cause may be local. The ML team's notes show no signals for this department.

35 of 36 other stores were below forecast in this department (median -45.8%), and all four Central Atlantic stores were too. The ML team's notes say the same season in earlier years was +4.9%, so this is not a normal seasonal pattern.

This store was -27.3% below forecast, while other stores were a median -8.1%. Only 2 of 4 other Central Atlantic stores were below forecast and none were flagged, so this drop is more local than the others.

34 of 38 other stores were below forecast (median -30.4%), suggesting a broad pattern. The Fed report on high summer temperatures and this week's slightly cooler weather are possible, but general, reasons.

report.not_found: I looked for a store-specific cause for these drops (such as stock, staffing, or local competition) and for any report that names these departments in this period, and found none that could be tied to this store.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Now, the remainder of our discussion today is focused on our core business which excludes fuel for comparative purposes, unless otherwise noted.Net sales were $12.2 billion, up 3.6 percent from last year. Our strongest divisional performance was in the West, with our strongest regional performance in the Great Plains, Mid South, and Mid Atlantic. Now I'd like to turn your attention to merchandising. There were three major themes during the third quarter: price investment, moderation of inflation, and new product introduction.

passages.section: Walmart U.S. Neighborhood Markets and Other Small Formats
passages.text: • Apparel includes apparel for women, girls, men, boys and infants, shoes, jewelry and accessories; and • Home includes home furnishings, housewares and small appliances, bedding, home décor, outdoor living and horticulture.

"We were pleased that our constant currency sales and operating income were both up approximately 7 percent for the third quarter," said Doug McMillon, president and CEO of Walmart International. "We gained market share in almost all of our markets, indicating that our underlying business is performing well. We are working hard to improve execution where it's needed, and we're ready with great merchandise and price investments for the fourth quarter." U.S. comparable store sales review and guidance The company reported U.S. comparable store sales based on its 13-week and 39-week retail calendar periods ended Oct. 26, 2012 and Oct. 28, 2011, as follows:

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

Retail Trade and Services Retail sales rose further overall. Contacts reported sales were a bit stronger relative to the prior reporting period. Discount chains and online retailers continued to outperform traditional department stores. At grocery stores, consumer spending was soft as shoppers continued to shift their purchasing decisions in favor of cheaper products. Contacts reported a strong pace for auto sales, significantly above the pace from the same period last year. Demand for used vehicles also remained robust.

report.summary: Department 31 Accessories is the largest gap, and it is shared: 36 of 42 other stores were also below the ML forecast that week, and all four other West Coast stores were too. Walmart overall was close to its forecast (-0.4%), so the pattern points to a category or regional cause more than a company-wide one, though none of the sources confirms why. The other flagged departments show a mix of shared and store-specific gaps, and no cause is verified.

findings.title: Accessories drop shared across many stores
findings.text: Dept 31 Accessories was below the ML forecast at 36 of 42 other stores, with a median of -25.5%. This store's -45.4% is well below that median, so the drop is larger here, but it is not unique to this store.

findings.title: Apparel category includes these departments
findings.text: The Walmart 10-K says "Apparel includes apparel for women, girls, men, boys and infants, shoes, jewelry and accessories" (P2). This matches Dept 31 Accessories and Dept 33 Girlswear, which both fall under the Apparel unit, so a category-wide shift in apparel is one possible explanation to check.

findings.title: Regional grocery softness reported
findings.text: The San Francisco Fed Beige Book says, "At grocery stores, consumer spending was soft as shoppers continued to shift their purchasing decisions in favor of cheaper products" (P5). This may relate to the grocery departments flagged here, but the report describes the district as a whole, not this store.

findings.title: Walmart overall near forecast that week
findings.text: All 45 stores were $44,210,995 against a forecast of $44,396,958 (-0.4%), and Store 12 as a whole was $922,671 against $924,521 (-0.2%). Walmart's quarter comparable sales were +1.5%. Store 12's flagged departments are therefore small gaps set against a store that is near its total forecast.

findings.title: Meat and Horticulture gaps look store-specific

findings.title: Calendar and weather show little change

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported modest increases in retail spending on a year-over-year basis, but many reported slower growth in recent months compared with earlier in the year; however, Boston and Cleveland reported sales as flat, and New York cited softer sales. There were a few reports that high summer temperatures negatively affected sales. Sales of big-ticket household goods were strong in the Richmond, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts, while sales were reportedly flat for home furnishings and major appliances in the San Francisco District. Boston reported that sales for furniture and electronics had slowed, and retailers in the New York District reported that home goods sales were weak. Reports from luxury-goods retailers were mixed.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.text: Hello, this is Carol Schumacher, vice president of investor relations for Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. Thanks for joining us today for our earnings call to review the third quarter of fiscal 2013. All information for this quarter, including our unit counts, square footage, and financial metrics, is available on our website. New address: stock.walmart.com. Please note that while we update unit counts on a monthly basis on our website, in the earnings discussion today, units and square footage are referred to as of the quarter end. Our press release is available on the website, and a full transcript of this call has already been posted there. Here's the agenda for today's call.

Consumer Spending Consumer spending improved with stronger than expected sales in June and was expected to strengthen further in the coming months. District retailers reported increased sales, particularly for seasonal items, mid-priced appliances, apparel, and fashion accessories. Several high-end retailers, however, commented that economic uncertainty had slowed demand for luxury items. Auto sales climbed sharply and were expected to remain solid for the next few months with more dealers offering sales incentives and discounts. Fuel-efficient cars sold well, while demand for large, expensive cars and trucks remained weak. Restaurant sales increased more than expected as both the number of diners and average check amounts edged up in June. Tourism activity ramped up with the start of the summer vacation season, though wildfires in Colorado hurt traffic in the Rocky Mountain region. District hotel owners reported a sharp rise in occupancy at higher average room rates and expected bookings to remain strong during the next three months.

EX-99.1 d440140dex991.htm PRESS RELEASE Press Release Exhibit 99.1 For Immediate Release Media Relations Contact Randy Hargrove 800-331-0085 Investor Relations Contact Carol Schumacher 479-277-1498 Pre-recorded conference call 877-523-5612 (U.S. and Canada) 201-689-8483 (All other countries) Call passcode: 9256278 Walmart reports Q3 EPS of $1.08, reaffirms top end of full-year EPS guidance; Company is well positioned for Q4 holidays Q3 Highlights : Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. (Walmart) reported third quarter diluted earnings per share from continuing operations of $1.08, within guidance of $1.04 to $1.09. This was an 11.3 percent increase from the $0.97 per share reported for the third quarter last year.

Agriculture and Natural Resources According to District reports, agricultural conditions were mixed largely because of severe drought conditions that affected the Midwest more than the rest of the country. Producers in the Chicago, St. Louis, and Kansas City Districts were all severely affected by the drought, with cotton, soybean, and corn crops particularly damaged. Cotton production in the Dallas District was also badly damaged, while the northern part of the Minneapolis District reported good corn, soybean, and wheat crops, and the San Francisco and Richmond Districts reported strong demand for their healthy cotton crops. Although nearly all agricultural commodity prices rose, higher feed costs led to reduced herd sizes and lower livestock prices in nearly all Districts reporting on livestock. Reports from the Richmond and Kansas City Districts indicated that farmland values have continued to rise, although contacts in the Kansas City District expected them to hold steady for the rest of the year. Farm incomes generally rose or stayed the same in the Minneapolis District.

report.summary: Three of the six flagged departments (Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear, Dept 56 Horticulture and Dept 6 Cameras) were also below the ML forecast at most other stores that week, so the pattern is shared by many stores and not only this one. Store 13 is also below its forecast in 46 of 69 departments, which suggests a wider store-level softness. Possible reasons include category-wide demand, regional conditions or local factors, but none has been verified.

findings.title: Outerwear, horticulture and cameras down widely
findings.text: In Dept 36 Outerwear & Swimwear, 35 of 36 other stores were below the ML forecast that week, with a median of -44.9%. In Dept 56 Horticulture, 34 of 38 other stores were below, and in Dept 6 Cameras, 28 of 39 were below. This points to a category-wide pattern that may be shared by many stores.

findings.title: Store 13 below forecast in most departments
findings.text: Across Store 13, 46 of 69 departments were below the ML forecast that week. The store total was $2,043,846 against a $2,102,510 forecast (-2.8%). This suggests a broader store-level softness, not only the six flagged departments.

findings.title: Seafood and cosmetics gaps look more local
findings.text: Most other stores were not below the ML forecast in Dept 83 Seafood (median +0.8%) or Dept 59 Cosmetics (median +0.4%). For these two departments, the gap at Store 13 is less shared, and no broad cause was found in the data.

findings.title: Two other regional stores also down
findings.text: In the Rocky Mountain region, Store 44 was -74.3% and Store 17 was -40.7% below the ML forecast in Dept 6 Cameras, and both were flagged. Only two other stores are in this region, so this is a small sample.

findings.title: Walmart overall was close to forecast
findings.text: Across all 45 stores that week, sales were $47,466,798 against a $47,656,239 forecast (-0.4%), and 20 of 45 stores were below. Walmart U.S. comparable sales for FY2013 Q3 were +1.5%, and the Aug 29, 2012 Beige Book said that "Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up." This does not point to a broad slump across Walmart.

Store 13 had 82°F against 80°F the prior four-week median, and local fuel was $3.51/gal against $3.58. These are general reports, not findings about this store.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

Retail Trade and Services Retail sales rose further overall. Contacts reported sales were a bit stronger relative to the prior reporting period. Discount chains and online retailers continued to outperform traditional department stores. At grocery stores, consumer spending was soft as shoppers continued to shift their purchasing decisions in favor of cheaper products. Contacts reported a strong pace for auto sales, significantly above the pace from the same period last year. Demand for used vehicles also remained robust.

passages.section: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms
passages.text: Walmart Study Finds Back-to-School Season Marks the New Year for Moms BENTONVILLE, Ark., July 18, 2012 /PRNewswire/ -- Walmart today announced the results of the "Walmart Class of 2012 Back-to-School Survey," which revealed that 76 percent of moms with children in kindergarten to 12th grade consider back-to-school a time for a fresh start over Jan. 1[1] – in fact, nine out of ten moms make back-to-school "resolutions" in preparation for the year ahead[2]. With 78 percent of moms planning to get organized[3] this new school year, Walmart today launched Classrooms by Walmart, an online compilation of thousands of classroom supply lists representing schools in all 50 states plus Washington, D.C., making it easier for moms to get their back-to-school supplies online and in Walmart stores.

passages.text: Consumer Spending Retailers report that sales activity has firmed somewhat since the last report. Two major retail chains report that sales in the region were on plan in July and ahead of plan in early August. Similarly a major retail mall in upstate New York reports some firming in sales, as well as shopper traffic, in July and early August, following lackluster business in May and June. Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down with the retreat in cotton prices earlier this year. Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region. Inventories are generally said to be at or slightly above desired levels.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

Similarly, weekly attendance and revenues at Broadway theaters were running ahead of comparable 2011 levels in August and early September but slipped well below year-earlier levels for the third week of the month. Finally, consumer confidence fell in August and was little changed at a low level in September, according to the Conference Board's monthly survey of residents of the Middle Atlantic states (NY, NJ, Pa).

Consumer Spending and Tourism Consumer spending was mixed but generally reported to be flat to up slightly over the latest reporting period. Retail sales were said to have improved modestly in the Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Minneapolis, and San Francisco Districts, while sales were characterized as flat to softer in the New York and Kansas City Districts. In general, retail sales were reported to be running only modestly ahead of a year ago. A number of reports noted various factors affecting sales, such as rising gasoline prices, political uncertainty, concerns about the "fiscal cliff" and weather. Atlanta and San Francisco noted that discounters have been outperforming traditional department stores. Cleveland reported that back-to-school merchandise sold well, while Chicago said that such sales were below expectations. Boston noted a pickup in furniture sales, Richmond cited brisk sales at building supplies stores, and San Francisco reported stronger demand at restaurants and food-service establishments.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q3 earnings call transcript
passages.section: And now I'll turn it over to Jeff for the financial details. Jeff…
passages.text: Our apparel business posted a low single-digit comp increase, making this the third straight quarter of positive comps. The consistency of our apparel business and focus on basics, especially in kids, ladies, and men's, continues to drive growth, despite the impact of a warm October across much of the country. We have worked hard on improving item quality, focusing on the elements that our customers appreciate, and are optimistic that our current trend will continue into the holiday season.

passages.source: Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript
passages.section: Now, let's turn it over to our operating segments. We'll start with Walmart U.S. Bill …
passages.text: Sales growth in the quarter was well balanced, with positive comps across all 3 geographic business units and in all of our store formats. Our 1.4 million associates did an outstanding job serving our customers, and I'm particularly pleased with the results we achieved during the key holiday events of Mother's Day, Father's Day and the Fourth of July. Despite a midweek holiday, July 4th sales, especially in key categories like food, significantly exceeded our expectations.

report.summary: Several flagged departments also sold below the ML forecast at many other stores that week, so part of this drop may be wider than Store 24. Walmart overall was also below forecast, and the Beige Book passages do not point to a clear cause for these departments. No store-specific cause was found in the data provided.

findings.text: Dept 35 Plus & Maternity was below the ML forecast at 26 of 36 other stores that week, with a median of -13.7%. Store 24's -33.3% is part of a wider pattern in this department, though the ML team's notes still flag it.

findings.text: Across all 45 stores that week, sales were $47,131,887 against a $48,409,634 forecast (-2.6%), and 35 of 45 stores were below forecast. No holiday fell in the week, and local fuel was $4.03/gal against $3.91 the prior weeks' median, which may have weighed on spending.

findings.title: Regional report mixed for apparel
findings.text: The Federal Reserve Beige Book of Aug 29, 2012 said that "Retail prices continue to be described as steady--including apparel prices, which had previously been expected to drift down." It also said "Stores in New York City have performed on par or modestly better than those in the rest of the region." These are regional comments, not findings about Store 24.

findings.title: Store-wide softness, not only flagged areas
findings.text: Store 24 had 55 of 71 departments below the ML forecast that week, and the store as a whole was $1,343,995 against a $1,414,320 forecast (-5.0%). Because the drop is spread across most departments, a single local issue is less likely to explain all seven flags.

passages.text: Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported modest increases in retail spending on a year-over-year basis, but many reported slower growth in recent months compared with earlier in the year; however, Boston and Cleveland reported sales as flat, and New York cited softer sales. There were a few reports that high summer temperatures negatively affected sales. Sales of big-ticket household goods were strong in the Richmond, Chicago, Kansas City, and Dallas Districts, while sales were reportedly flat for home furnishings and major appliances in the San Francisco District. Boston reported that sales for furniture and electronics had slowed, and retailers in the New York District reported that home goods sales were weak. Reports from luxury-goods retailers were mixed.

Consumer Spending and Tourism Most Districts reported that retail spending in July and early August was up compared with the previous Beige Book. New York and San Francisco noted strengthening sales compared with a softer May and June, although in San Francisco's case, the rise was only "a bit further." Philadelphia, Richmond, Minneapolis, and Kansas City reported stronger retail sales, while Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, and Dallas all said that sales were up "slightly." In the Atlanta District, most retail contacts reported slower sales, while Boston's retail contacts provided a mixed assessment.

passages.text: Most of our merchandising areas again delivered solid performance, though industry trends in electronics continue to impact the broader entertainment category. No report describes these specific departments at this store, and the ML team's own notes state its forecasts run high for most stores in these departments.
